title: SplitPane's keyboard resize clamps against the bound it is moving away from
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, one of three asked whether each component specification still describes the component that exists

evidence.verified: Reverting the fix fails exactly the new test and nothing else. `npx vitest run src/components/SplitPane.test.tsx` exits 1 on `clamps the keyboard resize when the handle sizes the right pane`, and exits 0 with the fix in place. The test drives a SplitPane whose left pane is flex-fill. It holds ArrowLeft six times against a 320px maximum and reads `aria-valuenow` 320, then holds ArrowRight twenty times against a 200px minimum and reads 200. Unclamped those reach 360 and 120. `npm run ci` exits 0 reporting every gate ran, with 625 tests passing where 624 passed before, visual:compare 94/94 at 0 differing pixels, and axe violations 0.

details:
`resolvePane` returns `direction: -1` when the left pane is the flex-fill one, because the handle then sizes the pane on its right (`src/components/SplitPane.tsx:45`).

The arrow handlers do not account for that sign. `SplitPane.tsx:107` computes `Math.min(max, currentWidth + step * direction)` for ArrowRight, and `:108` computes `Math.max(min, currentWidth - step * direction)` for ArrowLeft. With `direction` at -1, each key is clamped against the bound it is moving away from. Holding ArrowLeft grows the pane past `maxWidth` without limit, and holding ArrowRight shrinks it below `minWidth`.

The arrows are also inverted against the key table at `components/SplitPane.md:96`, which gives ArrowLeft as decrease and ArrowRight as increase.

Pointer drag clamps correctly at `SplitPane.tsx:137`, so only the keyboard path is affected. That is the accessible path, which makes it the worse half to have broken.

notes.text: Session agent confirmed every citation in this record against the tree at a374f2c before filing it.

Fixed by clamping between both bounds, which is what pointer drag already did. The arrow keys were not inverted after all: they move the handle, and the width that changes belongs to whichever pane is fixed. The key table said the arrows change a width without saying whose, so it now says. Handled in one pass with the SplitPane items in CUI-044 and CUI-047.
